note: Canonical cross-app contract for Rider, Driver and Admin. Frontend-only today; a future single backend implements it. Every app ships an identical copy under contracts/ and runs contract tests against it.

ids.trip: tripId (string). Never offerId. Legacy alias rideId is read-only during migration.
ids.offer: offerId (string). One trip has many offers.
ids.event: eventId (string), server-assigned, unique per committed change.

wire.time: RFC 3339 UTC with Z, e.g. 2026-10-19T08:30:00Z. Durations are integer seconds.
wire.money: Money { amountMinor: integer, currency: ISO-4217 }. No major-unit floats, no display strings on the wire.

location.Place: { address?: string, lat: number, lng: number } — pickup, dropoff, stops
location.GeoFix: { lat, lng, accuracy, heading?, speedMps?, moving?, measuredAt } — device GPS only; moving is the app's stopped/driving judgement (v0.5.0)
location.locationsException: v0.5.1 (CONTRACT.md §10): the bodies of POST /locations/autocomplete, /locations/geocode and /locations/reverse-geocode name coordinates latitude / longitude, as the rider app sends and reads them. This is the one exception to the lat / lng rule; POST /routes and everything else keep lat / lng.

wire.case: JSON keys camelCase; enum values snake_case.
wire.readOnlyPosts: v0.5.1: POST /locations/*, POST /routes and POST /telemetry/* are read-only or fire-and-forget calls, not mutations: they take no Idempotency-Key and the server must not require one. Telemetry also takes no bearer token (optional) and no standard headers (optional).

categories.note: Category ids come from the admin Pricing catalog; admins can add, delete and deactivate categories and the apps follow the admin catalog. These are the seed ids every app must know. labels are display only (the catalog's label wins). v0.6.0: child_seat (Child Seat) joins the seed; the rider app's former id kids is read as child_seat for one release, and the driver app's "Booster Seat" is the child_seat category.

paymentMethodAliases.note: Read-only aliases accepted for one release (v0.3 ids). Never sent.

zonePaymentMethods.note: Owner Q7 (final): every country offers exactly these methods, in this order; config paymentMethods is a subset. No swish, no d17. The wallet is not a method here: it is one balance per currency, used first (features.wallet, wallet.usedFirst).

languages.note: App languages (owner Q48/Q49). Admin sets the default per country for each app; the user can change it.

fareLines.note: fareLines[].code. rider: lines of the rider's fare (TripProjection.fare, Quote.total). driverOnly: lines the rider never sees or pays; shown to the driver and admin only (Offer, admin trip money).

aliases.note: v0.4 documents named the rider's pickup line pickup_pay; read it as pickup_fee for one release.

meaning.note: v0.5.1 (CONTRACT.md §3.5): what each rider line carries. Lines with amount 0 are left out, except base, distance and time (and fixed_route) which are always sent.
meaning.surge: ride part × (multiplier − 1); on base + distance + time only
meaning.minimum_adjust: raises the ride part to the category minimum (positive)
meaning.maximum_adjust: lowers the ride part to the category maximum, or to the booked fare when the rider ends early (negative)
meaning.fixed_route: a fixed route price instead of base + distance + time; no surge, minimum or maximum
meaning.waiting: waiting at pickup after the free wait, per second; 100 % the driver's, no commission
meaning.stop_waiting: waiting at each extra stop from the driver's arrived-at-stop to leaving-stop, per second, no free minutes (v0.7.1); 100 % the driver's, no commission
meaning.extras: v0.7.1: the one seat of a child_seat trip (childSeatFee once)
meaning.airport: v0.7.1: fees.airportPickup / airportDropoff when the pickup / drop-off lies in an airport zone (server decides)
meaning.app_fee: appFeePct of (ride part + extras); Movera keeps it
meaning.pickup_fee: the rider's fixed pickup fee (§3.2); Movera keeps it
meaning.rounding: total (rounded once to priceStep) − the sum of the other rounded lines; may be negative
meaning.outstanding_fee: an unpaid cash cancel / no-show fee from an earlier trip (FareLine.sourceTripId), added after the price step rounding; owed to Movera, never in driverEarnings (§3.7)
meaning.discount: unchanged from v0.5.0; promotions are off in the test week

transitions.note: declined, timed out or claimed elsewhere
v0.5.1: split from the v0.5.0 row (offered, requested); a live trip is accepted only from offered
a scheduled trip the driver claims early (the v0.5.0 row said so in its note; v0.5.1 makes it machine-readable)

admin direct assign (exclusive offer to one driver, kind=assigned) or radar group (up to 10 drivers, kind=radar); the driver still accepts. Locked once a driver accepts: from accepted on, assign is invalid_transition.
PIN check when the zone requires it
reassign: the trip goes back to dispatch, the cancel counts in the driver's rate
the reservation goes back out to drivers
already on the way: the scheduled trip is dispatched again like a live one
quote lapsed or no driver found in time
payment hold failed, zone closed, sweeps

ratingTransitions.when: trip completed, or (rider rating only) trip ended early by the rider: see ratingAllowed

ratingAllowed.note: Who may rate a trip once it is over, and after what. A rating is allowed when the rater, the trip's terminal status and (if given) the command that ended the trip all match one row; anything else is 409 invalid_transition. A plain rider cancel (command cancel) is never rated.

rules.note: the rider ended the trip early (POST /trips/{tripId}/end-early) and gets the normal rating screen

adminDispatch.note: Admin dispatch tooling (owner Q13-Q18). Both actions are the admin `assign` transition; the trip stays offered until one driver accepts, then the assignment is locked.

directAssign.note: Exclusive offer to one chosen driver: accept or decline. Counts as an exclusive offer for acceptance rate and auto-offline.

radarGroup.note: One offer per chosen driver, first to accept wins; the others get offer_withdrawn (claimed_elsewhere). The admin may send more groups while the trip is not locked.

driverBonus.note: Movera-paid extra for the driver ("add money to trip"). The rider never pays it. It is included in Offer.fare and Offer.driverEarnings as the driver sees them; TripProjection.fare (rider) never includes it. Above driver.driverBonus.defaultLimit the server answers 400 invalid_request ("adjust the limit in Pricing"); the limit itself can never exceed driverBonus.hardMax.

pickupPay.note: v0.5.0 (CONTRACT.md §3.2). Two sides. Rider: a fixed pickup fee per category, one amount for live rides (Radar and Exclusive), one for reservations, each on or off (null = off), in the rider's fare as the pickup_fee line; it never depends on the driver. Driver: Movera pays the drive to the pickup from its share, per category: tiered km ranges and an optional maximum per ride; the driver sees the total only (display total). The server works it out from the driver's location when the offer is made and sends it as Offer.pickupPay; the apps' own maths (fixtures/pickup_pay.json) is for demo offers and checks.
pickupPay.offerKindNote: offers[kind] switches each kind on or off (Admin Pricing › Pickup pay). scheduled = a reservation the driver took from the Scheduled rides list: never pickup pay. nextTrip = an offer while driving a rider: the leg is from the current drop-off.

ranges.note: PickupRange { fromKm, toKm: number|null, perKm: Money, perMin: Money }. The first starts at 0, each next one starts where the one before ends, only the last may be open (toKm null). A km is paid at the rate of the range it is in; a leg beyond a closed last range uses the last range. The minutes are split across the ranges in proportion to the km in each (0 km: all in the first range).
ranges.rounding: each range part: half_up(km × perKm) + half_up(minutes × perMin) in minor units; the parts add up; then min(total, maxPerRide)

riderFee.note: PickupPayRate.riderFee { live: Money|null, reservation: Money|null }; null = off. Added to the quote as the pickup_fee line; Movera keeps it.

pickupPay.moneySplit: rider pays fare (pickup_fee inside); driver gets driverEarnings + pickupPay + driverBonus; Movera keeps fare − driverEarnings − pickupPay − driverBonus, and covers it when negative

driverMotion.note: v0.5.0 (CONTRACT.md §3.3). The driver app decides stopped / driving from the device: moving when the speed is at least movingSpeedMps for hysteresisSeconds, stopped when below it for hysteresisSeconds. It sends the judgement as GeoFix.moving (and speedMps) in POST /driver/location and applies the offer limits itself at once; the server mirrors the latest fix's moving in Driver.moving and holds offers above the limit.
rules: no rider on board, moving: the full-screen Radar list cannot be opened while offers.radarApp.fullLockWhileDriving (it opens again once stopped); at most offers.radarApp.popupWhileDriving offer cards over the map when popupSplitByDriving, else popup
no rider on board, stopped: at most offers.radarApp.full in the list, offers.radarApp.popup cards over the map
rider on board: Exclusive offers only, at most offers.exclusiveWhileDriving.count at a time, never Radar (Q18); cards never cover navigation
the server never sends more open offers than the limit of the driver's current state; a held offer is sent when a slot frees or dropped when it expires

surge.note: v0.5.0 (CONTRACT.md §3.4). An admin surge may change over its time as a curve: points (atMin, multiplier) from 0 to the end, straight lines between them, applied in stepMinutes steps so the price never wobbles. The server prices new quotes from it; a quote keeps its multiplier (Quote.surgeMultiplier). Replaces nothing: a flat manual surge is a two-point curve. v0.6.0: the cap is set by the admin, at most capMax (6, the admin slider's top, owner 2026-10-27); every multiplier is also kept within the zone's pricing surge.maxMultiplier (CONTRACT.md §3.5). v0.7.1: the manual surge's maximum is its own slider value (cap = its highest point), at most capMax; pricing.surge.maxMultiplier no longer binds it.
surge.valueAt: value at minute m = curve value at floor(m / stepMinutes) × stepMinutes, rounded half-up to roundTo, clamped to [minMultiplier, cap]; null before startAt and from endAt on
surge.scope: zoneId plus categoryIds (empty = every category); one active schedule per zone and category; a new one replaces it

auth.note: v0.5.0 (CONTRACT.md §8). Token issuance for the rider and driver apps; the admin signs in with e-mail and password plus a second factor (out of this contract). Actor and ids come from the token.

otp.note: POST /auth/otp/request → { requestId, sessionId, expiresAt, retryAfterSeconds }; POST /auth/otp/verify { phone, sessionId, code } → tokens. A wrong code is 400 invalid_request (reason invalid_otp_code), an expired session 410 otp_expired, too many attempts 429 rate_limited.

auth.providerNote: POST /auth/provider { provider, idToken, app } signs in an account already linked to that Apple / Google identity (AuthTokens), or answers { code: PHONE_REQUIRED, linkToken, firstName?, lastName?, email? } for a new one: the app then verifies a phone with the linkToken on the OTP calls (the phone is confirmed once, the first time), the account is created linked, and the driver app prefills its details screen with the names and e-mail the provider gave (Apple gives them only the first time and may give a hidden relay e-mail; all stay editable). Unset provider keys on the server answer 503 unavailable (provider_not_configured).

tokens.access: JWT, short-lived (accessExpiresSeconds), bearer on every call
tokens.refresh: opaque, rotated on every POST /auth/refresh; a used or revoked one is 401 unauthenticated

testSignIn.note: Outside production the server seed lists test phone numbers; an OTP request for one of them sends no SMS and the fixed code signs it in. Production has no test numbers. The code below is the placeholder until the owner sets one.

devices.note: POST /push/devices { token, provider, platform, appVersion?, locale? } registers the device for push, keyed by token and actor; POST /push/devices/unregister { token } on sign-out. The same for rider and driver.

admin.note: v0.5.1 (CONTRACT.md §9), owner decisions 9 and 14 (2026-10-24): the admin panel signs in with e-mail and password through the server; this replaces "outside this contract" in auth.note for the admin. No second factor in v0.5.1.
admin.passwordHash: argon2id, server side; the password never leaves the sign-in and setup calls

reasons.invalid_credentials: 401 unauthenticated: unknown e-mail, wrong password or deactivated account, one generic answer
reasons.setup_link_expired: 410 otp_expired: the one-time link is older than setupLinkHours
reasons.setup_link_used: 410 otp_expired: the one-time link was used already

admin.lockout: failed sign-ins are slowed and then locked per e-mail and per address: 429 rate_limited with Retry-After
admin.secondFactor: none in v0.5.1. Reserved for later, additively: a sign-in answer { code: "SECOND_FACTOR_REQUIRED", challengeId } followed by a verify call; v0.5.1 servers never send it.
admin.superAdmin: role super: every permission is granted. v0.7.2 (owner 2026-10-28, one admin is enough everywhere): no action of any admin needs a second admin; AdminMe.approvalExempt is true for every admin.
admin.oneAdmin: v0.7.2 (owner 2026-10-28): ONE admin is enough for everything in the admin panel. Every admin with the operation's permission for that zone runs it at once (200 / 201, never 202 pending_approval): refunds, trip adjusts, config publishes and restores, surge Start/Stop, dispatch control and every other change; each is written in the audit. GET /admin/approvals stays to read approvals filed before v0.7.2; one still pending may be approved or rejected as before.

providerKeys.apple: APPLE_CLIENT_IDS (the app bundle ids / service id), tokens verified against Apple's public keys
providerKeys.google: GOOGLE_CLIENT_IDS (the OAuth client ids), tokens verified against Google's public keys

configVersion.note: v0.8.0 (owner 2026-10-27, "the server's version number counts"): the SERVER stamps version and publishedAt on every publish; whatever the admin sends in those two fields is ignored. version is strictly increasing per zone and document as the apps see it: a zone that served its country's standard (configDocs.standard) and then gets its own document continues above the standard's version. config_published carries the same version. Apps keep the last good document and ignore an older or equal version.

adminPermissions.note: v0.5.1 (CONTRACT.md §9): the admin panel's 34 permission ids (platform/team.ts). Every admin operation names one in x-permission; where v0.5.1 changed a v0.5.0 value, openapi.yaml keeps the old one under x-permission-v050. Roles: AdminRole; super has all of them.

v050.note: v0.5.0 x-permission values and what replaces them (per operation in openapi.yaml x-permission-v050)

configDocs.note: v0.5.1 (CONTRACT.md §6.2, §6.3). ConfigDocName values. app documents are served to the apps (GET /rider/config, /driver/config, config_published). serverOnly documents are published by the admin through the same draft / publish calls and the same version rule (configVersion), read only by the server and by admins with settings.read; the apps never get them. v0.8.0: country_rules is published per country only (configDocs.countryRules); the four zone documents may also be published per country as that country's standard (configDocs.standard).
mustMatch: RiderAppConfig.waiting and DriverAppConfig.waiting (the top-level terms) = pricing.categories[headline].waiting (economy, else the first category)
DriverAppConfig.offers.radarSeconds / exclusiveSeconds / radarOn / exclusiveOn = dispatch.radar.seconds / exclusive.seconds / radar.on / exclusive.on
configDocs.mustMatchNote: mustMatch binds the documents published for one zone. v0.6.0: the sample documents fixtures/config/rider_app_config.json and driver_app_config.json are aligned with fixtures/config/pricing_document.json (12.26 kr/min, Premium 16.90, no-show fee 65 kr) and reference_check.py checks the rule against them.
configDocs.publishPricing: v0.6.0 (owner 2026-10-27): publishing the pricing document keeps the app documents in step. In the same transaction the server writes the zone's live rider_app_config and driver_app_config again with waiting.byCategory (freeWaitMin, perMin, noShowAfterMin, noShowFee), the top-level waiting terms of the headline category, RiderAppConfig.pickupFee.byCategory and DriverAppConfig.pickupPay.byCategory[].riderFee taken from the new pricing document; every other field stays as published. Each app document whose values change gets the next version and publishedAt and sends config_published; one whose values are already equal is left as it is. A zone with no app document published yet gets none (the admin publishes the first one). An app document's draft, when there is one, takes the same values and its draft version goes up by 1 (an admin holding the old draft version gets 409 version_mismatch and reloads), so a later app publish does not undo them.
rules: country_rules
configDocs.countryOnlyNote: v0.8.1: empty; country_rules (configDocs.rules) is now published per zone or per country like the others.
configDocs.scope: v0.8.0: GET, PUT and POST …/publish on /admin/config/{doc} name exactly one of zoneId (the zone's own document) or country (ISO alpha-2; the country's standard). Both or neither → 400 invalid_request (reason scope_required). v0.8.1: country_rules too may name a zoneId (the zone's own tips and limits) or a country (its standard). A country scope is open to any admin who covers at least one zone of that country and holds the document's permission (owner 2026-10-27).
configDocs.standard: v0.8.0 (owner 2026-10-27): every country has one standard rider_app_config, driver_app_config, pricing and dispatch, set in the admin, in the country's currency. A zone with no own published document of a kind uses its country's standard of that kind: the server serves it (GET /rider/config, /driver/config) and prices and dispatches with it, with zoneId set to the zone's id and usesStandard: true; its version is the standard's version. A zone with its own published document never uses the standard. Publishing a standard sends config_published (app documents) for every zone of the country that uses it. A zone's first own publish gets version max(own live, standard live) + 1. A standard document carries zoneId "standard-<CC>" (e.g. standard-SE) and its country's currency, country and timeZone. GET /admin/config/{doc}?zoneId returns usesStandard: true and the standard as the draft's starting point while the zone has nothing of its own.
configDocs.countryRules: v0.8.1 (owner 2026-10-28: Tips & limits apply only to the zones chosen at the top; for the whole country the admin chooses all zones): tips, raiseSteps and driverBonus are the country_rules document { version, publishedAt, country, currency, tips: [AmountOption], raiseSteps: [AmountOption], driverBonus: { defaultLimit, hardMax } }, like the other documents published per zone (?zoneId, the zone's own) or per country (?country, the country's standard). A zone's rules are its own once published for it, else its country's standard (usesStandard: true); a zone with its own rules never uses the standard again until 'Go back to Standard' (useStandard, also for country_rules). Publishing a zone's own rules writes, in the same transaction, RiderAppConfig.tips / raiseSteps and DriverAppConfig.driverBonus of that zone's live and draft app documents; a zone that uses the standard app documents gets its own, copied from the standard with the new values (as publishPricing does), each changed one as its next version with config_published. Publishing the standard rules writes them into the standard app documents and into the own app documents of every zone of the country that has no own rules; zones with their own rules keep them. While a zone's rules (own or standard) are live, PUT and publish of that zone's app documents take those three fields from them, whatever the admin sent; the dispatch driver bonus limit of a trip is its zone's rules. The admin panel publishes to exactly the zones chosen at the top ('All zones' = every zone of the country it may work in, each as its own) and to the standard only when it is chosen.
configDocs.publishApproval: v0.8.0 (owner 2026-10-27, as refunds): no second admin. Any admin with the publish permission (settings.publish; dispatch.edit for dispatch; settings.publish for country_rules) publishes at once: 200 ConfigPublication, never 202. dispatch.approve and approval.decide no longer apply to config.
configDocs.useStandard: v0.8.0 (owner 2026-10-27): POST /admin/config/{doc}/use-standard { zoneId, expectedVersion } (the zone's draft version; same permission as publish; the admin confirms first) makes a zone with its own document use its country's standard again. The zone's own live document and draft are removed (every version stays in the history); the server re-stamps the standard as version max(standard live, the zone's own live) + 1 (a history row, the same content) so the zone's apps never see a lower version, and sends config_published to every zone using the standard. No standard published for the country → 409 conflict (reason standard_not_published); a zone already using the standard → 409 (reason already_standard).  v0.8.1: also for country_rules: the zone's own rules are removed and the standard rules are written into the zone's app documents (next version).
configDocs.countryRulesV080: v0.8.0 (replaced by v0.8.1): country_rules was published per country only and applied to every zone.

pricing.note: v0.5.1 (CONTRACT.md §3.5). The server prices every quote and fare from the zone's pricing document (admin Pricing, the order of quoteRide), with owner decisions 16-21 applied. Amounts are exact until they become a fare line. Cases: fixtures/fares.json.
order: ride part: a matching fixed route (fixed_route, no surge / minimum / maximum), else base + perKm × km + perMin × minutes

surge: ride part × multiplier, multiplier clamped to [1, 6] (the surge slider's top); the extra is the surge line. v0.7.1 (owner 2026-10-27, 'surge maximum = the value the admin chooses on the slider, no extra box'): each source carries its own maximum: the manual surge its slider value, a planned window its multiplier, smart surge its profile's cap; pricing.surge.maxMultiplier is deprecated and ignored
minimum: ride part raised to minimum (minimum_adjust); maximum: ride part lowered to maximum when not null (maximum_adjust)

extras, unsurged: waiting, stops, stop_waiting, extras (v0.7.1: a child_seat trip always includes one seat, its childSeatFee once; no other category has a seat fee), airport (fees.airportPickup when the pickup lies in a zone of kind airport, fees.airportDropoff when the drop-off does; the server decides, v0.7.1), reservation_fee (kind=scheduled)
pickup fee = riderPickupFee.live, or .reservation for kind=scheduled (null = none)
total = half_up((ride part + extras + app fee + pickup fee) / priceStep) × priceStep, rounded once
lines: each exact amount half_up to a whole minor unit; rounding = total − sum of the rounded lines (left out when 0)
outstanding_fee (§3.7) is added after the rounding: Quote.total / fare = total + outstanding
pricing.halfUp: half_up(x) = floor(x + 1/2) in minor units: a tie goes up (toward +∞), also on a negative line
pricing.waiting: waiting = Waiting.chargedSeconds / 60 × waiting.perMin, accrued per second after freeWaitMin (the driver app's rule; the admin calculator multiplies minutes, the same value for whole minutes). stop_waiting (v0.7.1, owner 2026-10-27: no free minutes at a middle stop) = Σ over stops of (leftAt − arrivedAt) seconds / 60 × stopWaitPerMin, from the driver's arrived-at-stop to leaving-stop (an open stop counts until the trip completes).

moneySplit.commissionBase: ride part + extras − waiting − stop waiting (owner decision 17: no commission on waiting; decision 18: the app fee and the pickup fee are Movera's and outside it)
moneySplit.driverEarnings: min(total before outstanding_fee, half_up(commissionBase × (1 − commissionPct / 100)) + waiting line + stop_waiting line)
moneySplit.moveraShare: Quote.total / fare − driverEarnings (app fee, pickup fee, commission, rounding and any outstanding_fee); TripProjection.commission carries it. Driver pickup pay and driver bonus are paid from it (§3.2).

pricing.quoteAndFare: The quote prices the server's own route (OSRM km and minutes; a client distance is a hint) with no waiting. The fare at completion is the same calculation with the quote's km and minutes, the quote's surge multiplier, the stops made and the waiting the trip had (Waiting.chargedSeconds, stop waits from the driver's arrive / leave taps), rounded once. A reservation (kind=scheduled) keeps the price of its booking: no surge in force later is added (owner 2026-10-27).
pricing.endEarly: owner decisions 8 and 19: ride part = base + km driven × perKm + minutes on board × perMin, × the booked surge multiplier, then minimum and maximum; no extras; + app fee + pickup fee. If that exceeds the booked fare (Quote.total plus route changes, without outstanding_fee) the ride part is lowered (maximum_adjust) to (booked − pickup fee) / (1 + appFeePct / 100), so the exact sum is the booked fare; then rounded once to priceStep. driverEarnings from that ride part.
pricing.surgeSource: first match: the zone's active surge schedule (§3.4, PUT /admin/zones/{zoneId}/surge: the manual Start/Stop), then the highest pricing.surge.scheduled window in force (v0.7.1: overlapping planned surges, the higher counts; the admin is warned on save), then smart surge when smart.enabled (v0.7.1: contract.json#smartSurge, off by default); else 1.0. Every source is clamped to [1, 6]; the maximum of each is the value the admin chose on its slider (manual surge, planned window, smart profile cap; v0.7.1, no separate maximum). The quote keeps its multiplier; a reservation keeps the price shown at booking (no surge added later).

requestExtras.note: v0.7.1 (owner 2026-10-27): the only priced thing the rider sends is fixedRouteId (QuoteRequest, repeated unchanged on CreateTripRequest, else 400 invalid_request quote_mismatch). Seats and airport are no longer sent: a child_seat trip always includes one seat, and the airport fees come from the airport zones (server).
requestExtras.fixedRouteId: the id of one of the zone's fixedRoutes: when it is a route of the quoted category the fixed_route line replaces the ride part (no surge, minimum or maximum); otherwise the category is priced normally, as in the admin calculator
requestExtras.seat: ONE seat fee (CategoryPricing.childSeatFee), only on child_seat: every child_seat trip includes one seat and adds the fee once in the extras line. The rider never chooses a number of seats. babySeats or childSeats above 0 (v0.6.0 fields, read for one release) on any other category: 400 invalid_request, reason seat_not_offered; on child_seat they change nothing. A pricing document with a seat fee on another category, or with babySeatFee, is 400 invalid_request (seat_fee_not_child_seat).
requestExtras.airport: the server looks up the pickup and the drop-off in the zones of kind airport (Zone.kind): the pickup inside one adds the priced zone's fees.airportPickup, the drop-off inside one its fees.airportDropoff (the airport line). airportPickup / airportDropoff sent by an older app are ignored.

pricing.maxMultiplierNote: v0.6.0: the highest surge an admin may choose is 6 (the demo's surge slider, SLIDER_MAX). v0.7.1 (owner 2026-10-27): there is no separate zone maximum: the slider's value is the maximum; pricing.surge.maxMultiplier is deprecated, may be absent and is ignored.
pricing.notInFormula: cleaningFee (charged afterwards with an admin adjust), tollsPassThrough (no tolls priced in v0.5.1)

dispatch.note: v0.5.1 (CONTRACT.md §3.6), owner decisions 6, 10, 22, 23, 24 and the technical defaults (2026-10-24). How the server finds a driver for a live trip in searching, from the pickup zone's dispatch document and its DispatchControl. Cases: fixtures/dispatch.json.
dispatch.skippedNote: test week, owner decision 10: these steps are skipped and change no timing

ranges.factors: at least one on with weight > 0
ranges.other: auto needs both modes on; manual main must be on; every on time rule needs from != to (HH:MM) and its mode on

dispatch.distance: km = round1(equirectangular distance × 111.32 × roadFactor); a driver finishing a ride: km from the drop-off. round1(x) = floor(x × 10 + 0.5) / 10
dispatch.eta: etaMin = max(1, round(km / pickupKmh × 60) + finishing.inMin), round = floor(x + 0.5)
dispatch.busy: busy = round1(waiting / max(1, free)) once at search start: waiting = trips in the zone in requested, searching or offered (the new one included); free = online drivers in the zone with no rider and no trip
dispatch.reasonCodes: Exclusive Offer.reasonCode: favourite when the favourite factor gave points; else finishing-nearby; else best-match for the top-ranked driver in range at that moment; else nearby
rules: mode at search start, first match: control.paused → no automatic offers; control.mode; the first on time rule (zone-local HH:MM in timeZone, [from, to), wraps midnight) whose mode is on; choose.how auto (both modes on) → radar when busy >= radarAbove else exclusive; else choose.main if on, else the mode that is on. choose.backup and rulesFrom are ignored (the pickup zone's document governs the search).

candidates at each offer, ranked again each time: eligible first (category allowed, km <= widest step, a driver on a ride only when finishing within finishing.withinMin and withinKm and the finishing factor is on), then score descending, km ascending, driverId ascending. Radar never goes to a driver with a rider; Exclusive does only when finishing.exclusive and exclusiveWhileDriving.on.

score = sum over the factors that are on of round(weight / (sum of on weights) × 100 × clamp01(ratio)): eta 1 − etaMin / etaFullMin; rating (rating − ratingFloor) / ratingSpan; acceptance pct / 100; cancel 1 − pct / cancelZeroPct; idle idleMin / idleFullMin; finishing 1 when finishing nearby; favourite 1 when the rider favourited the driver, favourite.on and km <= favourite.maxKm. A factor that does not apply still counts in the sum of weights.

Radar round: the top radar.drivers in range at the current step, all at once, for radar.seconds; the first accept wins (others claimed_elsewhere). Radar adds nobody to asked: a driver who declined or missed may see the trip again on a later round (owner decision 23).
Exclusive: one driver at a time, the best in range not yet asked, for exclusive.seconds; at most exclusive.drivers per step; each driver is asked once per search (asked). A decline moves on at once.

after a Radar round nobody accepted: widen (then widen or widen_then_exclusive, not at the widest step); else switch to Exclusive at the same step (then exclusive or widen_then_exclusive, exclusive on, not switched into before; tried = 0); else widen; else the steps are used up. After an Exclusive step: widen (widen, widen_then_radar; tried = 0); else switch to Radar (radar, widen_then_radar, radar on, not switched before); else widen; else used up. The start mode is not counted as switched into.
a round with nobody in range moves on at once (no time passes).

steps used up before the search end (owner decision 22, approved as "Radar every 15 s at the widest area, and Exclusive to any driver not yet asked"): the search never goes silent. Each repeat round at the widest step is: when exclusive.on and a driver in range has not been asked on Exclusive in this search (newly free drivers count), an Exclusive offer to the best such driver for exclusive.seconds; otherwise, when radar.on, a Radar round to the top radar.drivers in range for radar.seconds; otherwise wait radar.seconds (exclusive.seconds when Radar is off) and look again. Rounds go on until the search end.

search end = min(radius.maxWaitMin, the first on busy step) measured from search start (t = 0, when the trip enters searching). No new offer starts at or after the end; Offer.expiresAt = min(sentAt + seconds, search end). At the end the trip takes system expire (expired) unless a driver accepted.

rider-waiting steps: the on steps not skipped, sorted by afterMin (stable), each fires at afterMin × 60 s from search start if not after the search end; TripProjection.searchStep shows the latest. alert_admin: Live alert, offers go on. keep_waiting: the rider answers POST /trips/{tripId}/keep-waiting: wait → search end += extraMin × 60 and a busy step not fired yet moves to no earlier than the new end; stop → the normal free rider cancel; no answer → the search goes on (owner decision 24). busy: the search ends at that moment.

DispatchControl: paused stops new offers in running searches too (open ones run out); the waiting steps and the search end keep running. A forced mode applies to new searches only; forcing a mode that is off is 400 invalid_request (reason mode_off).

a free driver holds at most 1 open Exclusive; a driver with a rider at most exclusiveWhileDriving.count; a driver already holding one is skipped and does not count toward exclusive.drivers. Radar deliveries follow §3.3.
a driver cancel that sends the trip back to searching starts a new search (t = 0, new steps); the driver who cancelled stays in asked.

score inputs: acceptance and cancel rates over the last 30 days, rating as shown, fallbacks when there is no data; idleMin = minutes since the driver last became free or came online; favourites score 0 until the server has the data.

control.note: DispatchControl { zoneId, paused, mode: radar | exclusive | null, by, at, version } is live state, outside publishing. PUT /admin/zones/{zoneId}/dispatch-control (dispatch.edit). Pausing, forcing a mode, resume and back to rules apply at once for every admin with dispatch.edit (v0.7.2, one admin is enough).

dispatch.searchStep: TripProjection.searchStep { id, kind, message, extraMin: int | null, at } (rider view): the latest rider-waiting step that fired. Sent as trip_projection; it does not change version (like the after-cancel reason). raise_price and upgrade never appear in v0.5.1.
dispatch.offerTimers: DriverAppConfig.offers.radarSeconds, exclusiveSeconds, radarOn, exclusiveOn must equal dispatch.radar.seconds, exclusive.seconds, radar.on, exclusive.on of the same zone (contract.json#configDocs.mustMatch).

raisePrice.note: Owner decision 25 (2026-10-26): POST /trips/{tripId}/raise-price while searching or offered. fare += increase (rider_raise line); the whole raise goes to driverEarnings (Movera's share unchanged); open offers are withdrawn and a new search starts in which drivers who declined are asked again at the new price; version + 1. The new fare may not pass maxFactor × the quoted fare (400 invalid_request, reason raise_too_high). The raise_price waiting step stays skipped: the rider app offers the raise on its own schedule.

maps.note: v0.5.1 (CONTRACT.md §10), owner decision 4: address search through the server (Google Places / Geocoding), routes and arrival times from Movera's own OSRM. All of them are read-only POSTs or GETs: no Idempotency-Key.
maps.serverRoutes: the server routes quotes itself; QuoteRequest distance / duration from a client are hints and never priced

telemetry.note: v0.5.1 (CONTRACT.md §11). Fire-and-forget logs from the apps: no auth required (a bearer token is used when sent), no Idempotency-Key, X-Request-Id and X-Api-Version optional. 202 with an empty body.
telemetry.privacy: clients scrub e-mails, phone numbers and coordinates; the server scrubs again before storing
telemetry.limits: rate limited per address and device: 429 rate_limited; a body over maxBodyBytes is 400 invalid_request (reason payload_too_large)

liveDrivers.note: v0.5.1 (CONTRACT.md §12), owner decision 11: the admin live map reads driver positions from the server.
liveDrivers.keep: trip GPS traces are deleted after traceKeepDays; only each driver's latest position is kept beyond that

riderNearby.note: v0.5.2 (CONTRACT.md §13): the free cars near the rider, drawn on the rider's map while it chooses a ride. No driver id, name, plate or trip; positions rounded; the key changes every day.
riderNearby.who: drivers online and free (not on a trip, no accepted trip), with a fix not older than freshSeconds

driverOnboarding.note: v0.5.3 (CONTRACT.md §14), owner decisions of 2026-10-25: the driver app signs in with the phone and the code (§8) and then sends its details once (POST /driver/onboarding); the account waits on hold until Movera approves it. Two account types: a driver who works for a fleet, and a fleet (a company with cars and drivers; its owner may drive too). Documents are listed per country and account type and uploaded to the server for review in the admin panel. Tunisia is shown but not open yet.

accountStatus.pending: signed in, details not sent yet (the app shows the details screen)
accountStatus.on_hold: details sent, waiting for Movera (the app opens with the account on hold; the driver uploads documents, cannot go online)
accountStatus.active: approved by an admin (POST /admin/drivers/{driverId}/status); may go online with an approved vehicle

fleetCode.note: Made by the server when an admin approves the fleet; shown only to the fleet owner (GET /driver/fleet) and admins. A driver asks to join with the code plus the owner's full name and e-mail as registered; all three must match (one mismatch message, fleet_join_mismatch), and the owner then accepts or declines the request (fleetInvitations). An admin can make a new code (POST /admin/fleets/{fleetId}/code); the old one stops working at once.

vehicles.note: Fleet accounts own the cars (POST /driver/vehicles); an admin approves each (POST /admin/vehicles/{vehicleId}/review). A linked driver sees the fleet's approved cars (GET /driver/vehicles) and picks the one he drives (PATCH /driver/profile { vehicleId }). One car has one driver at a time: a car is in use while another driver has it picked and is online or on a trip (409 conflict, reason vehicle_in_use); picking a car another offline driver had moves it (that driver picks again before going online). A driver account that is not linked to a fleet has no cars (the app says the fleet's vehicle details are awaited).

payouts.note: Driver.payoutTo tells who is paid: fleet for a driver linked to a fleet (the fleet's bank; the driver sees his own trips and earnings, the owner sees every driver's earnings with GET /driver/fleet/earnings), self for a fleet account.

documents.note: kind file: uploaded with POST /driver/documents (multipart) and reviewed by an admin; acceptance: terms, accepted on POST /driver/onboarding (termsAccepted) and stored approved; admin_check: no file, an admin marks it approved (the session was held). required[country].driver are the person's documents (every account); required[country].fleet are the company's (fleet accounts; the fleet is approved on them, and the owner needs his driver documents too to go online himself); required[country].vehicle per car. Driver.requiredDocuments and Vehicle.requiredDocuments carry the lists so the app never computes them.

name.fr: Extrait Kbis ou avis SIRENE (moins de 3 mois)
Certificat d’inscription au registre des exploitants VTC

upload.note: Files are stored by the server (encrypted at rest, Europe) and read only through GET /driver/documents/{documentId}/file (the owner) and GET /admin/documents/{documentId}/file (documents.approve). fileUrl is that path, never a public link.

fleetInvitations.note: Owner decision 2026-10-25: joining a fleet is a two-sided invitation. driver_request: the driver asks with the code, the owner's name and e-mail (POST /driver/fleet/join); the owner accepts or declines. owner_invite: the owner invites a phone number (POST /driver/fleet/invite); a driver with an account gets it at once, one without gets it the moment he signs up with that number; he accepts or declines. Either side may cancel its own. The other side is told in the app (GET /notifications, kind fleet_invitation; a badge on Home and My fleet) and by one SMS. An admin sees pending invitations on the fleet and may accept or cancel one. Accepting links the driver (Driver.fleet) and closes every other pending invitation of his.

smsText.sv: {fleet} bjuder in dig till sitt åkeri i Movera. Öppna appen för att svara.
smsText.fr: {fleet} vous invite dans sa flotte Movera. Ouvrez l’application pour répondre.
smsText.en: {fleet} invites you to its fleet in Movera. Open the app to answer.

smsTextRequest.sv: {driver} vill gå med i {fleet} i Movera. Öppna appen för att svara.
smsTextRequest.fr: {driver} veut rejoindre {fleet} dans Movera. Ouvrez l’application pour répondre.
smsTextRequest.en: {driver} wants to join {fleet} in Movera. Open the app to answer.

fleetInvitations.appLink: the SMS to a number without an account ends with the app's install link (deploy setting)

outstandingFee.note: v0.5.1 (CONTRACT.md §3.7), owner decision 7: an unpaid cash cancel or no-show fee puts the rider in minus (Rider.outstanding) and is added to the next trip as the outstanding_fee line.
rules: Cancellation.feeStatus owed while unpaid; Rider.outstanding is the sum of the owed fees
every quote and the fare of the next trip carry outstanding_fee (FareLine.sourceTripId = the trip that owes it) while it is open
cleared (feeStatus paid) when a cash trip that carries it completes and is paid; a trip that carried it but did not complete leaves it owed
the driver of the original trip gets their share at once (an earnings entry, waiting.driverSharePct for a no-show); Movera carries the risk
on the next trip the line is cash the new driver collects (in cashCollected) but not in their driverEarnings: it is owed to Movera

accountDeletion.note: v0.5.1: POST /account/deletion (rider) answers 202 { status: requested }; the server erases the account on its own schedule (legal retention, open payments).

configDefaults.note: Defaults for the per-zone config fields (CONTRACT.md §6). Admin exports them where no setting exists yet; apps fall back to them when a document lacks a field or has a bad value. Money is in the country's currency. v0.5.0 adds offers, pickupPay and surge. v0.5.1 adds pricing (SE, the admin's Stockholm prices) and dispatch (the admin's zone defaults). v0.5.6: missedExclusiveBeforeOffline (DriverAppConfig.offers.autoOffline.missedExclusive) goes from 3 to 10 (owner decision 35, 2026-10-26).
configDefaults.noShowAfterMin: equals the category freeWaitMin (owner Q41): the no-show button appears when the free wait ends

offers.note: DriverAppConfig.offers limits (v0.5.0, CONTRACT.md §3.3). Admin Dispatch › Modes; every field optional on read.

pickupPay.note: DriverAppConfig.pickupPay and RiderAppConfig.pickupFee defaults (v0.5.0, CONTRACT.md §3.2). Placeholder amounts until the owner sets the real ones in Admin Pricing › Pickup pay: the rider fee is off (null) with these suggested amounts, the driver gets the first km free then the headline category's rate; other categories come from Admin.

reservations.note: DriverAppConfig.reservations (CONTRACT.md §6). Every field is optional on read: a missing or invalid field keeps this default. Admin ride type ids map normal->normal, airport->airport, long->longTrip, premium->comfortPremium, event->event; Admin lateBackupAfterMin is offlineBackupAfterMin. v0.4.2: there is no leaveNow switch any more (Leave now always opens the trip); a leaveNow field in an older document is ignored. on is the zone switch for every driver (= features.scheduledRides); with Driver.scheduledRides (per driver) it decides who gets new reservations, CONTRACT.md §6.1.

configDefaults.promoCap: null until Admin sets a cap for the country (no default decided)

pricing.note: PricingDocument defaults (v0.5.1, CONTRACT.md §6.2): the admin panel's Stockholm prices (zonePricing.ts defaultZoneBook), SEK minor units (öre); a full Z001 document is fixtures/config/pricing_document.json. Smart surge off (owner decision 21), the surge maximum 3 (the admin may set up to 6), stops 3 free minutes (decision 20). Other countries: the admin converts (FR × 0.095, TN × 0.3). v0.6.0: babySeatFee and childSeatFee only on child_seat.

SE.airportZones: ARN and BMA: base and minimum × 1.3, airport pickup 6500, drop-off 3000

dispatch.note: DispatchDocument defaults (v0.5.1, CONTRACT.md §6.3): the admin panel's defaultZone for a city zone (Z001-Z009 identical; fixtures/config/dispatch_document.json is Z001). Airport zones: radar.drivers 8, radius.steps [3, 6, 10].

waiting.message: Drivers are busy. Raise your price to be picked up faster.
A Priority or Comfort car can come sooner. Upgrade?
We are looking for a driver for you.

rules: reject sequence < 1 or blank tripId
drop a seen eventId or sequence <= last seen
a gap (sequence > last + 1) is accepted and triggers a resync
after a terminal lifecycle status only afterTerminal kinds are accepted
a location event never replaces the cached projection
resync: GET /trips/{tripId} then GET /trips/{tripId}/events?after={sequence}

errors.shape: { code, message, requestId, retryable, reason?, projection? }
errors.reason: optional machine-readable detail under a code (snake_case), e.g. invalid_request + invalid_phone, invalid_otp_code, invalid_otp_session; never shown to users as is

headers.X-Request-Id: sent by clients, echoed by the server

cancelFees.note: v0.8.0 (owner 2026-10-27): DriverAppConfig.cancelFees.driverSharePct, set in Admin › Dispatch per zone: the driver's share of a rider's cancel fee, 0–100, default 100. Movera keeps the rest.

bookingSnapshot.note: v0.8.0 (owner 2026-10-27): a booked trip keeps ALL its rules from booking time (POST /trips). The server keeps on the trip: the pricing document (version and scope) it was quoted with, the category's cancel fee rule (live or reservation by Trip.kind, from RiderAppConfig.cancelFees, else the built-in default), DriverAppConfig.cancelFees.driverSharePct, the category's waiting terms (free wait, per minute, no-show after, no-show fee), DriverAppConfig.waiting.driverSharePct (no-show share) and driverShareWaitPct. A later publish never changes a booked trip; fixtures/settings_flow.json#snapshot.

autoOffline.note: v0.8.0 (owner 2026-10-27): a driver goes offline after offers.autoOffline.missedExclusive (default 10) Exclusive offers of live trips in a row that were declined or expired. Only kind=exclusive offers of live trips sent while the driver was free count; an Exclusive offer sent while the driver is on a trip never counts; Radar, assigned and reservation (scheduled) offers declined or expired never count. ANY accepted offer (Exclusive or Radar, any kind) and going online set the count back to 0. Both the server (it sets onlineStatus offline and marks the offer event driverOffline: true) and the driver app enforce it; fixtures/settings_flow.json#autoOffline.
neverCounts: exclusive sent while on a trip

safety.note: v0.7.0 (CONTRACT.md §15, owner safety part 1 decisions 2026-10-27). SOS from the rider or the driver and the server's 'car lost' alarm become incidents the admin takes, solves or calls a false alarm. The apps open the phone's emergency call (112) themselves AND send the SOS to Movera; afterwards they show only 'SOS sent' (no later update).

sos.note: One open SOS incident per trip: a second SOS on the same trip (any key, either side) returns that incident. The body carries the phone's GPS once; the admin also sees the car's latest position (driverPosition, from POST /driver/location).

safety.escalationNote: An sos or driver_silent incident not taken within escalateAfterSeconds raises incident_escalated: from then on every signed-in admin gets its events (before: only admins with incidents.read whose zones cover the incident's zone). No SMS when nobody is online.

driverSilent.closesWhen: driver positions come back (resolved by the system, resolution 'position back')

stopWaits.note: v0.7.1 (owner 2026-10-27, CONTRACT.md §3.8): waiting at a middle stop has no free minutes; the driver app reports each stop.
stopWaits.arrive: POST /driver/trips/{tripId}/stops/{stopIndex}/arrive { expectedVersion }: the assigned driver, trip in_trip or approaching_dropoff (else 409 invalid_transition, not_on_trip), stopIndex 0-based into TripProjection.stops; sets stops[i].arrivedAt (server time); version + 1, trip_projection. Again on the same stop: 409 invalid_transition (stop_already_arrived). Stops are taken in order: arriving at i while an earlier stop has no arrivedAt is 409 (stop_out_of_order).
stopWaits.leave: POST /driver/trips/{tripId}/stops/{stopIndex}/leave { expectedVersion }: sets stops[i].leftAt; before arrive: 409 invalid_transition (stop_not_arrived); twice: 409 (stop_already_left). version + 1.
stopWaits.charge: stop_waiting = Σ (leftAt − arrivedAt) seconds / 60 × stopWaitPerMin; an arrived stop with no leftAt counts until complete. A stop the driver never arrived at counts 0.

smartSurge.note: v0.7.1 (owner 2026-10-27): smart surge as the admin demo's Surge tab describes it, run by the server per zone; OFF until the admin switches pricing.surge.smart.enabled on. Applies to every category of the zone. v0.7.2 (owner 2026-10-28): free drivers are only those in the zone now.
smartSurge.ratio: every checkEveryMin minutes: ride requests created in the zone in the last checkEveryMin minutes ÷ free drivers in the zone. v0.7.2 (owner 2026-10-28): a free driver is online (not on a trip, online_status online) AND their latest GPS fix lies inside the zone AND it reached the server less than freshFixSeconds ago (the same drivers Dispatch counts as free); a zone with none counts as 1.
smartSurge.profile: the first non-default profile from the top whose days and windows match the zone's local time wins; else the isDefault profile. Outside activeFrom–activeTo (equal = all day) smart surge is 1.0.
smartSurge.target: the multiplier of the last step whose ratio ≤ the measured ratio (1.0 below the first step), kept within the profile's cap (at most 6)
smartSurge.rules: up: the target must hold for holdMin minutes before it is applied; down: one step at a time; between two changes at least cooldownMin minutes; stops (1.0) when the target stays 1.0 for stopAfterMin minutes. Paused while a manual or scheduled surge runs.

pricingHistory.note: v0.7.1 (owner 2026-10-27): the admin's Pricing › History, Restore and Undo last publish.
pricingHistory.list: GET /admin/config/{doc}/history?zoneId&cursor&limit (settings.read): newest first, ConfigHistoryEntry { version, publishedAt, publishedBy, note?, action: publish | restore, restoredFrom?, document }
pricingHistory.restore: POST /admin/config/{doc}/restore { zoneId, version, expectedVersion, note? } (the publish permission): publishes that version's document again as the next version (action restore, restoredFrom), with every effect of a publish (§6.2 app documents for pricing). Undo last publish = restore the version before the live one. A version not in the history: 404; the live version: 409 invalid_transition (already_live).
pricingHistory.audit: one audit row per pricing publish or restore: action config.publish, details { doc, zoneId, version, restoredFrom?, appDocuments: [{ doc, version }] } (the app documents the publish rewrote)

categoryCatalog.note: v0.7.1 (owner 2026-10-27): one catalog of car types for every country and zone (admin Pricing › Manage categories); each zone switches a category on or off in its pricing document.
categoryCatalog.entity: CategoryDef { id, label, line: { sv, fr, en } (the sub-line under the name, e.g. 'Up to 6 seats'), seats, builtIn, sort, archivedAt?, archivedBy?, archiveReason?, restoreUntil? }
categoryCatalog.routes: GET /admin/categories (settings.read); POST /admin/categories, PUT /admin/categories/{categoryId}, POST /admin/categories/{categoryId}/archive { reason }, POST /admin/categories/{categoryId}/restore (settings.publish)
categoryCatalog.archive: Delete = archive for restoreDays days, then gone. Refused while trips of the category are booked and not finished: 409 invalid_transition (category_in_use). Archiving switches the category off (enabled: false) in every zone's live pricing document (a new version each) and removes it from the catalog the apps get.
categoryCatalog.restore: within restoreDays: back in the catalog with its old prices, switched off in every zone; later: 409 invalid_transition (restore_expired)
categoryCatalog.apps: RiderAppConfig / DriverAppConfig catalog.categories[] gain line?: { sv, fr, en }; the server fills label, line and seats from the catalog and leaves out archived categories when it serves the documents. The rider app shows line under the name.

premium.fr: Voitures haut de gamme, meilleurs chauffeurs

child_seat.fr: Voiture avec siège bébé ou enfant
child_seat.en: Car with a baby or child seat

categoryCatalog.seedLinesNote: The admin demo's sub-lines for the seed categories (Manage categories), in the panel's sv / fr / en words; the server seeds the catalog with them.

surgeLive.note: v0.7.2 (owner 2026-10-28): the admin's Pricing › Surge tab shows only real numbers from the server: the surge now per zone (map, list, alerts), the demand chart, the rider price check and the surge timeline. No invented values: what the server cannot give is shown 'Not connected yet'.
surgeLive.samples: Each minute the server's surge check stores one SurgeSample per open zone (whether smart surge is on or not): { zoneId, at, requests (ride requests created in the zone in the last minute), freeDrivers (as contract.json#smartSurge.ratio), ratio (requests in the last checkEveryMin ÷ freeDrivers, as smart surge measures it), multiplier, source }. Samples are kept 8 days.
surgeLive.now: GET /admin/surge/now?zoneIds=Z1,Z2 (settings.read; zones outside the admin's scope are left out; no zoneIds = every zone in scope) → { at, zones: ZoneSurgeNow[] }. ZoneSurgeNow { zoneId, multiplier, source: manual | scheduled | smart | off, until?, scheduleId?, profileId?, requests, freeDrivers, ratio, checkedAt? }: multiplier and source exactly as a quote made now would get them (contract.json#pricing.surgeSource, before a category filter); requests, freeDrivers and ratio from the newest SurgeSample.
surgeLive.history: GET /admin/zones/{zoneId}/surge/history?hours=1..24&bucketMin=5|10|15|30|60 (settings.read; defaults 6 and 10) → { zoneId, from, to, bucketMin, points: SurgePoint[], priceCheck: PriceCheck, timeline: SurgeTimelineItem[] }.
surgeLive.points: SurgePoint { at (bucket start), requests (sum in the bucket), freeDrivers (average, rounded), ratio (average, 0.1), multiplier (highest in the bucket) }, oldest first; a bucket without samples is left out.
surgeLive.priceCheck: PriceCheck { windowMin: 60, saw, left, leftPct }: saw = quotes of the zone made in the last 60 minutes with surgeMultiplier above 1.0; left = those of them no trip was created from; leftPct = round(100 × left ÷ saw), 0 when saw is 0.
surgeLive.timeline: SurgeTimelineItem { at, kind: manual_start | manual_stop | scheduled_start | scheduled_end | smart_change | smart_end, multiplier, previous?, by? (the admin of a manual surge; 'smart' / 'scheduled' otherwise), profileId?, effect? }, newest first, the last `hours` hours (at most 50). Made from the samples (a change of multiplier or source) and the zone's surge schedules (who started or stopped it). effect, on a start or a rise, compares the 30 minutes after it with the 30 minutes before: { drivers (free drivers after − before, average), ridesPct (round(100 × (trips created after − before) ÷ max(1, before))), leftPct (the price check of the 30 minutes after) }; left out while the 30 minutes after are not over.

driverSurgeMap.note: v0.7.2 (owner 2026-10-28): the driver app shows surges ONLY as coloured zones on the Home map. No text, no number and no money on the map; the driver never sees the multiplier.
driverSurgeMap.route: GET /driver/surge-map (driver) → { at, zones: DriverSurgeZone[] }: the open operating zones of the driver's country whose surge now (as GET /admin/surge/now, before a category filter) is above 1.0. DriverSurgeZone { zoneId, level: low | medium | high, bounds: { south, west, north, east } } (the zone's rectangle). Never the multiplier.
driverSurgeMap.levels: low: multiplier above 1.0 and below 1.5 (×1.1–×1.4); medium: 1.5 to 2.5 inclusive; high: above 2.5. A zone at 1.0 is not listed (no colour).
driverSurgeMap.colours: low #FFC79E (light orange), medium #FF8A3D (orange, the demo's 'Hög bonus' colour), high #E5482B (red); fill about 40 % opacity with a 2 px edge of the same colour.
driverSurgeMap.refresh: the app asks while online on Home: on going online, then every 60 s, and when the app comes back to the front; it keeps the last answer when a call fails; offline it shows no colours.
driverSurgeMap.tip: The top bar's waiting tip 'Hög bonus i närheten' / 'Forte majoration à proximité' / 'High boost nearby' (no money, no number, no zone name) shows while the driver's position is inside a listed zone or less than 3 km from its rectangle, any level. The old '+{kr} kr i {zone}' tip is removed.

surgeNoticeRemoved: v0.7.2 (owner 2026-10-28): drivers get NO surge notice. pricing.surge.notifyDrivers is deprecated and ignored, POST /admin/zones/{zoneId}/surge/notify is gone (404) and the server sends no surge_started notification. The driver sees surges only as coloured zones on the Home map (contract.json#driverSurgeMap).
